defect_summary: Follow-up to BFF-GOVERNANCE-EVIDENCE-REDACTION-SWEEP-001, whose independent reviewer recorded two out-of-contract findings: (1) the same discarded-identity pattern exists in control_loops/router.py (9 handlers call _read_identity(authorization) and discard the return value) and in core/app_factory.py's inline settings handlers (2 handlers call extract_identity(authorization) and discard it); (2) GovernanceService.committee_projection returns linked_evidence unredacted on the committee detail route despite already receiving identity as a parameter. This task audits all 9 control-loops handlers plus the 2 settings handlers plus the committee detail route, redacts every surface whose response structurally carries evidence-ref-shaped content, and documents why the remaining surfaces carry none.

shared_helper_extraction.reason: The task brief explicitly requires reusing governance/router.py's existing fail-closed capability-resolution wrapper (previously a private closure named _safe_redact) rather than duplicating it into control_loops/router.py. Added the wrapper (safe_redact_evidence_refs) and a generic top-level list-field redaction helper (redact_evidence_field_items, mirroring governance/router.py's pre-existing _redact_evidence_field_items) to models.py.
shared_helper_extraction.governance_router_change: governance/router.py's _safe_redact is now a two-line delegation to the shared safe_redact_evidence_refs(); behavior is unchanged (verified by the full, unmodified 33-test test_governance_evidence_redaction_sweep.py suite still passing byte-for-byte).
shared_helper_extraction.governance_service_change: governance/service.py's committee_projection now calls the same shared safe_redact_evidence_refs() (via self.redact_evidence_refs/self.capabilities_for_identity, its own existing DI-injected collaborators) instead of copying linked_evidence unredacted. GovernanceService._fail_closed_redact_evidence_refs (the default injected when no canonical redact_evidence_refs is wired) now delegates to models.fail_closed_redacted_refs instead of maintaining its own separate copy of the same withhold-everything loop.
shared_helper_extraction.control_loops_router_change: control_loops/router.py gained two new optional constructor parameters (redact_evidence_refs, capabilities_for_identity) with the same DI defaults as governance/router.py (models.redact_evidence_refs / lambda identity: []), wired through core/app_factory.py exactly like the governance router already is.
shared_helper_extraction.settings_router_change: core/app_factory.py's create_settings_router gained the same two optional parameters (redact_evidence_refs, capabilities_for_identity), wired at the single settings mount site; get_settings/export_settings now redact a top-level evidence_refs field via redact_evidence_field_items() (fixes the corrected P1 finding above).
shared_helper_extraction.models_fail_closed_capability_fix: models.safe_redact_evidence_refs's own except-branch (triggered when the injected redact_fn itself raises) previously withheld every ref with only {ref_id, redacted, reason} -- dropping required_capability even for a ref whose evidence kind (e.g. metric) is known. Extracted the kind/capability resolution shared by redact_evidence_refs into models._resolve_evidence_kind_and_capability() and added models.fail_closed_redacted_refs(), which both this except-branch and GovernanceService._fail_closed_redact_evidence_refs now call, so a fail-closed withhold reports the correct required_capability whenever the ref's kind is resolvable, and 'unknown' only when it genuinely is not -- matching acceptance rule 4 (redacted + required_capability + reason on every withheld ref) instead of silently dropping the field on this one exception path.

regression_coverage_added.harness: Builds the real create_control_loops_router(), create_governance_router(), and create_settings_router() directly (never imports main), wired exactly like core/app_factory.py: redact_evidence_refs=models.redact_evidence_refs, capabilities_for_identity=auth.policy.capabilities_for_identity, extract_identity=auth.policy.extract_identity. No class-level monkeypatching of domain services -- minimal read-store doubles (_ControlLoopsSweepStore, _CommitteeSweepStore) plus a real, tempdir-backed SettingsStore supply populated, production-shaped fixture rows with mixed alert/metric/job evidence_refs (operator role holds risk.alert.read but lacks metric.read and job.read, so a mixed-refs fixture exercises partial redaction on every fixed surface, not just all-or-nothing). A _call_with_supported_kwargs() helper filters constructor kwargs by the target's live signature so the same builder functions run unmodified against an unmodified base checkout (see terminal_commands_and_results below) instead of erroring on an unexpected-kwarg TypeError.
coverage: OODA packets list + detail: low-capability identity redacts the metric/job refs while the alert ref stays visible and unredacted evidence_refs==[] items pass through untouched; full-capability identity (admin role) sees the exact original unredacted evidence_refs payload, not merely a zero count.

v5 intervention detail: low/full-capability pairs plus a fail-closed test (capabilities_for_identity raising -> every ref withheld with required_capability set, not merely a blunt reason-only stub).

v5 interventions list: a baseline test proving InterventionRecord's fixed Pydantic schema strips evidence_refs at the wire regardless of identity or capability -- documents the NO_OP_DOCUMENTED verdict rather than asserting a redaction that cannot structurally occur.

Control-room aggregate: low-capability identity redacts embedded intervention and sentinel evidence_refs (4 total across both embedded lists) while full-capability identity sees both sets fully visible and redacted_evidence_count==0.

Loop inventory list baseline: populated (non-empty) production-shaped response asserting no evidence_refs/linked_evidence field exists, documenting the NO_OP_DOCUMENTED verdict live rather than only in prose.

Loop inventory detail baseline: fetches a real loop_id from the populated list response and requests its detail directly (never a 404 or a fabricated id), asserting the same no-evidence-field verdict on the actual production-shaped detail record.

Downstream-health baseline: injects a monitor double whose get_state() returns real populated data (overall_ok=true, a populated target probe row, meta.source=bff_downstream_health_monitor) -- not the previous version's uninjected {overall_ok: null, targets: {}, meta.source: missing} shape, which proved nothing about the populated production response.

Settings get/export: low-capability identity redacts a mixed evidence_refs field mixed into a real SettingsStore bundle while unrelated sections stay intact; full-capability identity sees the original unredacted evidence_refs; a fail-closed test for capabilities_for_identity raising, covering both GET /api/v1/settings and GET /api/v1/settings/export independently (six tests total).
Governance committee detail: low/full-capability pairs plus a fail-closed test for the previously-unredacted linked_evidence field.

acceptance_notes.fail_closed: Confirmed by test_v5_intervention_detail_fails_closed_when_capabilities_unresolvable, test_committee_detail_fails_closed_when_capabilities_unresolvable, test_settings_get_fails_closed_when_capabilities_unresolvable, and test_settings_export_fails_closed_when_capabilities_unresolvable -- when capabilities_for_identity raises, safe_redact_evidence_refs() substitutes an empty capability set, so every capability-gated ref is withheld (each carrying redacted:true and its own required_capability from models.RedactedEvidenceRef) rather than disclosed. A separate fail-closed path -- safe_redact_evidence_refs()'s own except-branch, triggered when redact_fn itself raises rather than the capability lookup -- previously dropped required_capability entirely; models.fail_closed_redacted_refs() now resolves it from the same evidence-kind map whenever the ref's kind is known (fixes the P2 finding against models.py lines 744-755).
acceptance_notes.never_widens_disclosure: No change to models.redact_evidence_refs, EVIDENCE_CAPABILITY_MAP, or any role/capability mapping in auth/policy.py; only route handlers/service methods that previously discarded identity or skipped redaction now route their payload through the pre-existing canonical redactor.
acceptance_notes.no_duplicate_symbols_or_routers: The fail-closed capability-resolution wrapper exists in exactly one place (models.py::safe_redact_evidence_refs); governance/router.py's former private copy was replaced with a delegating call, not left as a second implementation. No new router, store, or fallback path was created; no symbol is defined twice.
acceptance_notes.redaction_after_pagination: Verified for GET /bff/ooda/packets (dedicated multipage test) -- redaction is applied to response['items']/response['data'] after in-router page slicing (_page()), not to the full unpaginated dataset.
acceptance_notes.bff_final_007_shape_match: Every withheld ref in this task's tests asserts redacted:true, required_capability, reason=="insufficient_capability", and each fixed surface's meta reports redacted_evidence_count -- produced entirely by the unmodified models.redact_evidence_refs/RedactedEvidenceRef (BFF-FINAL-007, commit 4a14129b9).
acceptance_notes.list_vs_detail_verified_separately: list_v5_interventions and its sibling detail route were audited and tested independently, surfacing a genuine structural difference between them (response_model-enforced schema on the list route vs. raw pass-through on the detail route) rather than assuming identical treatment -- the exact failure mode the task brief warned against (a prior sweep misclassified a detail route as safe using a list/empty baseline).

cross_router_and_residual_gaps.in_scope_and_fixed: All 9 acceptance-listed control-loops surfaces, both app_factory settings surfaces, and the governance committee detail route were audited; every surface carrying evidence-ref-shaped content was redacted, every surface without one was verified against a populated baseline and documented as NO_OP_DOCUMENTED.
cross_router_and_residual_gaps.no_further_discarded_identity_evidence_s: GET /bff/v5/sentinel/findings (the list route, not in the acceptance contract) already threads identity through for tenant scoping and is out of this task's declared scope; not modified.
